question.:question/problem:
Find where the normal line to the curve $y=-4\sqrt{x}+3x-2$ at the point with $x$-coordinate $4$ intersects the $y$-axis.

The intersection is $(${{field-1}}$,$ {{field-2}}$)$. Give exact values.
question.:question/worked-solution:
First find the point on the curve.

$$
f(4)=-4\sqrt{(4)}+3(4)-2=2.
$$

The normal passes through $(4,2)$.

Rewrite the radical or reciprocal using powers, then differentiate.

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(x)&=- 4 x^{\frac{1}{2}} + 3 x - 2, \\f'(x)&=3 - \frac{2}{x^{\frac{1}{2}}}=3 - \frac{2}{\sqrt{x}}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope and take its negative reciprocal to find the normal slope.

$$
\begin{aligned}
m_t=f'(4)&=3 - \frac{2}{\sqrt{(4)}}=2, \\m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}&=-\frac{1}{(2)}=- \frac{1}{2}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Use point-slope form through $(4,2)$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-(2)&=- \frac{1}{2}(x-(4)), \\y&=- \frac{x}{2} + 4.
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $y$-axis, $x=0$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
y&=- \frac{1}{2}\cdot 0+(4), \\y&=4.
\end{aligned}
$$

The intersection is $(0,4)$.

f(x)&=- 2 x^{\frac{1}{2}} - 2 x, \\f'(x)&=-2 - \frac{1}{x^{\frac{1}{2}}}=-2 - \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope and take its negative reciprocal to find the normal slope.

$$
\begin{aligned}
m_t=f'(1)&=-2 - \frac{1}{\sqrt{(1)}}=-3, \\m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}&=-\frac{1}{(-3)}=\frac{1}{3}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Use point-slope form through $(1,-4)$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-(-4)&=\frac{1}{3}(x-(1)), \\y&=\frac{x}{3} - \frac{13}{3}.
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $x$-axis, $y=0$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
0&=\frac{1}{3}x+\left(- \frac{13}{3}\right), \\x&=13.
\end{aligned}
$$

The intersection is $(13,0)$.

question.:question/problem:

question.:question/worked-solution:
First find the point on the curve.

$$
f(4)=4\sqrt{(4)}+2(4)-2=14.
$$

The normal passes through $(4,14)$.

Rewrite the radical or reciprocal using powers, then differentiate.

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(x)&=4 x^{\frac{1}{2}} + 2 x - 2, \\f'(x)&=2 + \frac{2}{x^{\frac{1}{2}}}=2 + \frac{2}{\sqrt{x}}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope and take its negative reciprocal to find the normal slope.

$$
\begin{aligned}
m_t=f'(4)&=2 + \frac{2}{\sqrt{(4)}}=3, \\m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}&=-\frac{1}{(3)}=- \frac{1}{3}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Use point-slope form through $(4,14)$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-(14)&=- \frac{1}{3}(x-(4)), \\y&=- \frac{x}{3} + \frac{46}{3}.
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $y$-axis, $x=0$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
y&=- \frac{1}{3}\cdot 0+\left(\frac{46}{3}\right), \\y&=\frac{46}{3}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The intersection is $(0,\frac{46}{3})$.
